questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Functions of Clothing' refers to.
questions.a: Clothing works on three fronts: protection from weather, injury and hazards; modesty as society defines it; and communication -- status, role, occasion and personality announced through dress. Decorative enhancement runs alongside these as people use clothes for beauty.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Functions of Clothing'.
questions.a: Clothes shield, cover and speak -- protection, modesty, communication and adornment in one garment.

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Factors Influencing Selection of Clothes' refers to.
questions.a: What people choose to wear is decided jointly by age and body build, climate and season, occasion and activity, fashion trends, income and the care the garment will need. Psychological factors -- conformity and individuality -- pull the choice in opposite directions at once.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Factors Influencing Selection of Clothes'.
questions.a: Every purchase is a compromise -- body, climate, occasion, money, fashion and care all file their claims.

concepts.title: Clothing Needs Across Ages: Children, Teens and Elders

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Clothing Needs Across Ages: Children, Teens and Elders' refers to.
questions.a: Clothing needs shift across the life span: infants want soft, washable, safe fabrics without tight trims; children need tough, free-for-play clothes; adolescents chase fashion and fit; elders prize easy opening, warm layers and comfort. Each stage pairs its physiological realities with its social expectations.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Clothing Needs Across Ages: Children, Teens and Elders'.
questions.a: Dress follows development -- softness for infants, sturdiness for children, style for teens, ease for elders.
